title: Skills Gateway Fastbridge 12-day Onboarding Playbook
summary: Compact, role-agnostic 12-day onboarding playbook designed for high-velocity hires (associate to senior IC). Combines an interview rubric for final-stage calibration, a prioritized day-by-day activation schedule, and a lightweight skills verification matrix to accelerate time-to-impact while keeping ramp risk low.
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is built for rapid assimilation of new hires into small product or infra pods where early autonomous contribution matters. It balances speed with safety: short, measurable milestones; early access gating; and a lightweight skills verification loop that flags need-for-support before week 2 ends.

Scope / target roles:
- Primary: Associate/Senior ICs across engineering, infra, and platform teams.
- Secondary: Technical PM and Solutions Engineer hires with a code-adjacent onboarding path.

Hiring plan notes (pre-acceptance):
- Offer window: 72 hours preferred; include 1:1 with hiring manager scheduled within 48hrs of accept.
- Preboarding packet (to send within 24hrs of signed offer): credentials checklist, Day0 agenda, buddy intro, minimal repo list, and quick-read architecture map (1 pager).
- Hardware & software order: prioritize laptop build + org membership day -2. If device not available, request remote shadowing plan.

Interview rubric (final loop calibration) — single-sheet scoring model:
- Dimensions (score each 1–4):
  - Technical correctness (can reason to solution): 1=major gaps, 2=partial, 3=good, 4=robust
  - System design / tradeoffs (scale, reliability): 1=not considered, 2=basic, 3=comprehensive, 4=insightful
  - Product sense & prioritization: 1=missing, 2=surface-level, 3=clear tradeoffs, 4=strong advocacy
  - Communication & collaboration: 1=unclear, 2=some clarity, 3=structured, 4=engaging/explains to others
  - Learning velocity & ownership signals: 1=low, 2=moderate, 3=high, 4=exceptional
- Pass threshold: average >= 2.75 and no dimension below 2.
- Tie-break guidance: prioritize learning velocity and communication when deciding between near-equal candidates.
- Calibration prompt examples (for final on-site/loop):
  - Tech correctness: "Implement or pseudocode a prefix-skipping cache and explain complexity tradeoffs."
  - System design: "Design a KV-cache routing layer for multi-tenant inference; highlight failure modes and mitigation."
  - Product sense: "Given a 20% latency improvement plan that increases cost 10%, how do you prioritize rollout?"

Scoring rubric record template (to live in interview notes):
- Candidate name | role | loop date | interviewer | scores per dimension | short note (2–3 lines)

Offer-to-Day0 checklist (ops):
- HR packet completed and returned
- Laptop assigned or remote plan documented
- Okta and org SSO accounts created (day -1)
- Slack invite + channel(s) pre-added
- Repo access (read) granted to key team repos
- CI/CD visibility + telemetry dashboards permission (viewer)
- Buddy assigned and calendar invite sent

12-day onboarding schedule (high-priority tasks only):
- Day 0: Welcome + access verification (okta, email, Slack), hardware check, HR admin, 30m with hiring manager on goals, 15m with buddy; simple repo build assignment (run tests locally).
- Day 1: Team onboarding (owners and product context), run first local dev loop, join team standup; assign first tiny-ticket (bugfix or doc tweak).
- Day 2: Deep-dive architecture read + walkthrough with engineer owner (30–60m), live pairing on first ticket (pair 60–90m).
- Day 3: Shadow on-call rotation review / SLO and runbook orientation (if applicable), complete first ticket and submit PR.
- Day 4: Instrumentation & CI orientation, add a small telemetry assertion to PR, review PR feedback rituals.
- Day 5: Mini-demo: share first PR outcomes in team sync; retro 1: what went well / blockers (15m).
- Day 6: Start role-specific learning module (2–3 micro-lessons total); second ticket with slightly larger scope.
- Day 7: Cross-team intro meetings (observability, infra, product); pair on cross-cutting task.
- Day 8: Skills verification checkpoint 1: manager + buddy sync; review learning module progress and unblock.
- Day 9: Small ownership project kickoff (1-week scope) and clear success criteria set.
- Day 10: Midpoint demo prep; feedback session with manager (30m).
- Day 11: Continue project; invite two stakeholders to review design.
- Day 12: Skills verification checkpoint 2: demo project outcomes, calibrated rubric filled; set 30/60/90 goals.

Skills verification matrix (week 2 artifacts to collect):
- Evidence items (attach as links or PRs): 1) working PR merged or in review, 2) small design doc or architecture note, 3) test/telemetry change, 4) retrospective note summarizing blockers.
- Manager uses matrix to mark: "Green (owns small scope)", "Yellow (needs pair support)", "Red (requires remedial plan)".

Buddy checklist (first 12 days):
- Day -1: Introduce via Slack and share quick-start repo list and pointers.
- Day 0: 30m intro (team culture, working norms), help verify dev environment.
- Daily (days 1–5): 30m pairing or review time; aim to unblock the first PR.
- Day 6–12: 2x weekly check-ins (30m) focused on goals and social integration.
- End of Day 12: Submit buddy summary (3 bullet highlights + 1 risk flag) to hiring manager.

Access & security gating guidance:
- Least-privilege principle: grant code read access at Day0, write after first PR merge or manager sign-off.
- Emergency access path: SRE on-call + sec-approvals channel for expedited access (documented in linked_artifacts).
- Secrets & data access: require manager sign-off + audit log request; provide sample masking patterns for test data.

Manager's short checklist (during first 12 days):
- Day 0: set 3 concrete goals for 12 days and align on priority ticket backlog.
- Day 4: one-on-one to review first PR and pair feedback.
- Day 8: skills checkpoint; decide go/no-go for independent write perms.
- Day 12: finalize 30/60/90 plan and assign primary mentor for 90-day follow-up.

Evaluation & go/no-go criteria at Day12:
- Go (green): merged PR + demonstrated independent debugging + clear plan for next 30 days.
- Partial go (yellow): merged PR but needs closer pairing on core subsystem; plan created + weekly check-ins.
- No-go (red): no working PR or consistent access/communication failures; initiate remediation plan (30-day targeted support).

30/60/90 deliverable template (manager & hire):
- 30d: own a small feature/bug cycle end-to-end and present results + metrics.
- 60d: reduce cycle time or triage backlog for the chosen component, demonstrate measurable improvement or documentation.
- 90d: lead a small roadmap slice or cross-team integration with stakeholder alignment.

Learning modules (micro-curriculum):
- Core infra: repo map, test harness, CI flows (30m reading + 60m guided lab).
- Observability: dashboards, SLOs, alerting playbook (20m reading + 45m walkthrough).
- Deploy flow: canary / rollback, where to look for failures (20m + practical checklist).

Communication norms & cultural primers:
- Async-first: encourage PR descriptions with context and expected outcomes.
- Meeting etiquette: pre-read at least 24hrs when requesting cross-team feedback.
- Review style: opinionated, kind, and actionable (use features request template).

Open questions / risks to triage:
- Hardware shortages in APAC region — contingency remote pairing plan required.
- Fastbridge pace might overwhelm some junior hires; flag indicators for early slowdown.

Appendix: sample interview notes template (copy/paste friendly)
- Candidate: _____
- Role: _____
- Loop date: _____
- Interviewer: _____
- Scores: Tech / Design / Product / Communication / Learning = __ /__ /__ /__ /__
- 3-line summary: _____
- Recommendation: Strong hire | Hire with coaching | No hire

Closing note:
This playbook is intentionally compact and opinionated. The goal is to standardize the first 12 days so hiring managers and buddies can run a consistent experiment: find gaps fast, reduce ambiguity for new hires, and create early wins that build confidence. Feedback loop: drop comments on the linked_confluence page (CONFLUENCE-4321) or ping people-ops in #people-ops for iteration.
